commentary_segments.text: For an average value for V L of 10 V, it becomes E B clear that decreasing the offset or increasing the CMRR is the same design task. If an offset can be expected of about 10 mV, as for many MOST differential pairs and opamps, then a CMRR of approximately 60 dB can be expected. If, on the other hand, the offset is 10 times smaller, as for bipolar opamps, then the CMRR is 20 dB higher as well. If the offset is trimmed down to the mV level, then the CMRR increases accordingly. Note however, that a CMRR of 120 dB can only be reached provided the offset is trimmed down to 10 mV.
